findings.message: Only part of the supersession fix is a class fix. firstAt is described as 'first deployed', but it reads each environment's latest non-voided deployment. listReleases picks those with `distinct on (release_id, environment_id) ... order by at desc`. firstAt also counts a stage with any status, failed included, as a deployment. So a release that was redeployed or retried, or that only failed, can hide the release that is actually Live. The rule for 'has reached a stage' now also exists twice: firstAt has its own test (`s.status && s.at`) next to standing(), which the old code used through `standing(o).last`. The two can disagree (B4). Fix: decide supersession from the other release's earliest successful deployment. Either have listReleases return a first_deployed_at (min(at) where status = 'deployed' and not voided), or build it from standing(). Then add table rows for a failed-only newer release and for a retried Dev deployment.
findings.scenario: 1) HRI v0.9.2 deployed to Prod on Oct 1. v1.0.0's only Dev deployment fails on Oct 5 (status 'failed'). firstAt(v1.0.0) = Oct 5 > Oct 1, so v0.9.2 drops off the Active map and the only row left is the failed v1.0.0. 2) v2 deployed to Dev on Sep 28, then redeployed to Dev on Oct 3. firstAt is Oct 3 > v1's Prod on Oct 1, so v1 counts as superseded even though v2 was first deployed before v1 shipped.

findings.message: The comment '0009 may already be applied' only covers databases that applied the original 0009 (the one with `shipped`). Round 1 (fd15dfe) edited 0009 to remove `shipped`, and this round edits 0009 again to put it back. A database migrated at round 1 has weekly_stat without `shipped`, so 0010's unconditional `drop column shipped` fails and the migration chain stops there. Also, if the runner checksums applied files, 0009 has changed under it twice. Fix: don't edit 0009 again; make 0010 `drop column if exists shipped`.
findings.scenario: A dev or CI database migrated at fd15dfe (0009 without shipped) runs the migrations at 7cad3c6. `alter table delivery.weekly_stat drop column shipped` fails with 'column "shipped" does not exist', so delivery.clock_pin is never created and every page that calls today() fails.

findings.message: The shared e2e global setup in apps/web, which the platform team owns, now writes straight into a delivery table with raw SQL. That ties the platform-wide setup to the delivery module being installed. With delivery removed or disabled, `delivery.clock_pin` does not exist and global setup fails for every e2e suite. Fix: seed the pin through a delivery fixture or test helper owned by the module, or skip it when delivery is not installed.
findings.scenario: AMAX_MODULES_DISABLED=delivery (or modules/delivery removed): global-auth throws 'relation "delivery.clock_pin" does not exist' and no e2e test runs.

findings.message: delivery.clock_pin is a test-only pin that lives in the production schema. It has no service, no audit trail, no expiry, and no on-screen sign that it is active. A leftover or mistaken row freezes 'today' for a real tenant's charts, 'Released this month' and the release map, with nothing on screen to show it. Consider showing the pinned date wherever it is used, or limiting pins to test or demo tenants.
findings.scenario: A row left in clock_pin for a live tenant makes 'Released this month' and the week charts stay on that date indefinitely.

findings.message: The README says the fixtures follow fixtures.md except for the shipped series. This round also moves the 'Login hotfix' from HRI-104 (no release) to an FLT proposal in a new FLT v1.7.3 release. That is a second deviation in project, key and release, and the README doesn't mention it. Document it or keep the hotfix in its fixtures.md project.

The supersession fix still covers only one ordering: the other release's first deployment comes after this one's Prod. When two releases overlap, the newer one can be deployed to an early stage before the older one reaches Prod. Its firstAt is then earlier than the older one's prodAt, so the older Live release is never marked superseded, even after the newer one reaches Prod. Fix: also treat a Live release as superseded when another release of the same project reached Prod later (compare live.at values), or when another release's latest deployment comes after this Prod deployment. Add rows for overlapping releases to the Active-map table.
findings.scenario: Same project, now=2026-10-16. v2 goes to Dev on 2026-09-28, v1 goes to Prod on 2026-10-01, v2 goes to Prod on 2026-10-06. onActiveMap returns [v2, v1], so both show as Live on the map, but only v2 is current in Prod.

findings.message: The 'latest' marker is drawn on the last non-null point. When the final weeks have no roll-up, the marker sits on an earlier week and reads as the current value. Fix: draw the marker only when the last label has data.
findings.scenario: data [3,5,null]: the highlighted end marker is drawn on W41 while the chart ends at W42, which has no data.
